question.text: A straight line <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> with equation <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> meets the circle with equation <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math> at <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> in the first quadrant. A line through <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo></math> perpendicular to <math><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> cuts the <math><mi>x</mi></math>-axis and <math><mi>y</mi></math>-axis at <math><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> respectively. The area (in sq. units) of the triangle <math><mi>O</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></math> is (where, <math><mi>O</mi></math> is the origin)

solution.text:
Slope of l1=12
Slope of l2=-2
Equation of l2 is y=-2x-10

⇒y+2x=20
Hence, P and Q are 10,0 and 0,20
Area of ∆OPQ=12×10×20=100 sq. units
